text_changes.before: Robust refinement of compact regions across workflows and external sections
text_changes.after: Robust refinement of compact regions across parameter settings and external sections

text_changes.before: Gains for compact regions stabilized over successive refinement rounds. From four to six rounds, mean best-IoU calculated with equal weight across samples ranged from 0.270693 to 0.270741 in development and from 0.343897 to 0.344037 externally. These narrow ranges showed that the final overlap gains were not confined to a single stopping point (Supplementary Tables S20 and S25).
text_changes.after: Gains for compact regions stabilized over successive refinement rounds. From four to six rounds, mean best-IoU calculated with equal weight across samples ranged from 0.270693 to 0.270741 in development and from 0.343897 to 0.344037 externally. These narrow ranges showed that the final overlap gains were not confined to a single stopping point (Supplementary Tables S20 and S25). Across expression weights from 0.70 to 0.90 and accepted-area retention from 95% to 100%, all 30 prespecified configurations had positive mean gains for every workflow and sample. Size 1–10 gain ranged from 0.1096 to 0.1179, with minimum workflow gains from 0.0665 to 0.0813 (Fig. 5b; Supplementary Table S31).

text_changes.before: RadarST exceeded random selection matched for both modification burden and geometry in both cohorts, supporting candidate prioritization beyond relabeling burden. Mean gains stayed positive across the evaluated settings for the number of refinement rounds and after omission of any external section. In external evaluation, selection that accounts for component properties reduced the fraction of loss events calculated with equal weight across samples from 5.85% to 4.45% and maintained positive mean gains across all 14 upstream workflows. The corresponding average best-IoU gains were 0.0948 for RadarST and 0.0893 for ordering by molecular score, with minimum workflow gains of 0.0183 and 0.0308, respectively (Supplementary Table S24).
text_changes.after: RadarST exceeded random selection matched for both modification burden and geometry in both cohorts, supporting candidate prioritization beyond relabeling burden. Mean gains stayed positive across the development parameter neighborhood, across the evaluated settings for the number of refinement rounds and after omission of any external section. In external evaluation, selection that accounts for component properties reduced the fraction of loss events calculated with equal weight across samples from 5.85% to 4.45% and maintained positive mean gains across all 14 upstream workflows. The corresponding average best-IoU gains were 0.0948 for RadarST and 0.0893 for ordering by molecular score, with minimum workflow gains of 0.0183 and 0.0308, respectively (Supplementary Table S24).

text_changes.before: We assessed sensitivity to iteration count by evaluating complete maps after zero through six refinement rounds. Each stopping point used the same trained models, features and rules for selecting actions (Supplementary Tables S20 and S25).
text_changes.after: We assessed sensitivity to iteration count by evaluating complete maps after zero through six refinement rounds. Each stopping point used the same trained models, features and rules for selecting actions (Supplementary Tables S20 and S25). We additionally evaluated all 30 combinations of five initialization expression weights (0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85 and 0.90) and six accepted-area retention fractions (95%, 96%, 97%, 98%, 99% and 100%) in development. Models, candidate identities and the six-round refinement rule were unchanged. The main analysis used an expression weight of 0.80 and 97% retention (Supplementary Table S31).

text_changes.before: Figure 5. Candidate selection, refinement burden and sensitivity analyses. Candidate prioritization is evaluated using matched controls evaluated by complete writeback, while modification burden and summaries obtained by omitting one section at a time describe the resulting maps. Numerical results for matched random and molecular controls are provided in Supplementary Tables S19 and S24. Results for different numbers of conditional refinement rounds are provided in Supplementary Tables S20 and S25.
text_changes.after: Figure 5. Candidate selection, refinement burden and sensitivity analyses. Candidate prioritization is evaluated using matched controls evaluated by complete writeback, while modification burden and summaries obtained by omitting one section at a time describe the resulting maps. Numerical results for matched random and molecular controls are provided in Supplementary Tables S19 and S24. Results for different numbers of conditional refinement rounds are provided in Supplementary Tables S20 and S25. Panel b shows the 30 combinations of expression weight and retention during initialization (Supplementary Table S31). The outlined cell marks the 0.80 weight and 97% retention. Panel d shows the 312 maps with nonzero modification. Ten maps with zero modification and zero gain lie at the origin, outside the shown range. Cohort means include all 322 maps.
